- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 10–20%.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast lows by 10–20%.
- After a sharp spike in sentiment or price, model often overshoots; apply a 15–25% downward correction to the immediate next period.
- Model frequently underreacts to mean reversion in sentiment cycles; if sentiment swings sharply, adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day average of recent history.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights early sentiment signals; dampen initial forecast values by 5–15% if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows a clear trend (e.g., rising or falling), model often fails to match; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction, but cap deviation at ±15% of recent 7-day average.
